framingShots.Extreme Wide Shot (EWS): Shows a vast landscape or environment. The subject is barely visible or very small in the frame. Used to establish location and scale. Perfect for epic, sweeping scenes.
framingShots.Wide Shot (WS): Shows the full subject and their surroundings. The subject is clearly visible but the environment is also important. Great for showing action and context.
framingShots.Full Shot (FS): Shows the entire subject from head to toe. The subject fills most of the frame. Used to show body language and physical actions clearly.
framingShots.Medium Long Shot (MLS): Frames the subject from knees up. Shows more detail than a wide shot while maintaining environmental context. Common in dialogue scenes.
framingShots.Medium Shot (MS): Frames the subject from waist up. The most common shot in filmmaking. Perfect for conversations and showing upper body gestures.
framingShots.Medium Close-Up (MCU): Frames from chest up. Emphasizes facial expressions while showing some shoulder and upper body movement. Great for emotional scenes.
framingShots.Close-Up (CU): Frames the face, filling most of the screen. Reveals detailed emotions and reactions. Creates intimacy and focuses viewer attention.
framingShots.Extreme Close-Up (ECU): Shows a very small detail (eyes, mouth, hands, objects). Creates intense focus and dramatic emphasis. Often used for important plot details.
framingShots.Cowboy Shot: Frames from mid-thigh up, named after Western films showing gun holsters. Popular in action scenes and character introductions.
framingShots.Over-the-Shoulder Shot (OTS): Camera positioned behind one subject looking at another. Essential for dialogue scenes, creates spatial relationships between characters.
framingShots.Two Shot: Frames two subjects in the same shot. Shows their relationship and interaction. Common in conversations and romantic scenes.
framingShots.Three Shot: Frames three subjects together. Useful for group dynamics and conversations involving multiple people.
framingShots.Point of View Shot (POV): Shows what a character sees from their perspective. Puts the audience in the character's position. Creates immersion and empathy.
framingShots.Insert Shot: A close-up of an important object or detail. Draws attention to specific elements crucial to the story (a watch, letter, weapon, etc.).
framingShots.Establishing Shot: Usually a wide shot that shows the location and sets the scene. Tells the audience where and when the action takes place.
framingShots.Master Shot: A continuous wide shot covering an entire scene. Provides spatial context and can be intercut with closer shots.
framingShots.Cutaway Shot: Briefly shows something outside the main action. Used for transitions, hiding cuts, or adding context.
framingShots.Reaction Shot: Focuses on a character reacting to something. Shows emotional responses and helps tell the story through facial expressions.
framingShots.Low Angle Shot: Camera positioned below the subject, looking up. Makes subjects appear powerful, intimidating, or heroic. Adds drama and authority.
framingShots.High Angle Shot: Camera positioned above the subject, looking down. Makes subjects appear vulnerable, weak, or small. Creates sympathy or shows dominance.
framingShots.Bird's Eye View: Directly overhead shot looking straight down. Provides a unique perspective, shows patterns, or creates disorientation. Very distinctive look.
framingShots.Worm's Eye View: Extreme low angle from ground level looking up. Creates dramatic emphasis and makes subjects appear monumental or imposing.
framingShots.Dutch Angle / Canted Angle: Camera tilted on its axis, creating diagonal horizon lines. Suggests unease, tension, disorientation, or psychological distress.
framingShots.Eye Level Shot: Camera at the subject's eye level. Most neutral and natural perspective. Creates equality between viewer and subject.
framingShots.Hip Level Shot: Camera positioned at hip height. Often used in Westerns and action scenes. Creates a grounded, ready-for-action feeling.
framingShots.Knee Level Shot: Camera positioned at knee height, looking slightly up. Makes subjects appear taller and more imposing.
framingShots.Ground Level Shot: Camera placed directly on the ground. Creates unusual perspective and can make ordinary objects appear larger.
framingShots.Aerial Shot: Shot taken from aircraft or drone, high above the scene. Shows large-scale geography and movement. Creates spectacular establishing shots.
framingShots.Long Shot (LS): Similar to wide shot, shows subject in full with significant environment. Emphasizes the relationship between character and setting.

cameraMovements.Pan (Left/Right): Camera rotates horizontally on a fixed axis. Follows action side to side or reveals environment. Smooth and natural movement.
cameraMovements.Tilt (Up/Down): Camera rotates vertically on a fixed axis. Reveals height, follows vertical action, or shifts attention from ground to sky.
cameraMovements.Zoom In: Lens magnifies to make subject larger without moving camera. Draws attention and creates focus. Can build tension or emphasize importance.
cameraMovements.Zoom Out: Lens widens to show more of the scene. Reveals context, creates distance, or shows isolation. Can create surprise reveals.
cameraMovements.Dolly In: Camera physically moves closer to subject on tracks or wheels. More immersive than zoom. Creates intimacy or builds tension.
cameraMovements.Dolly Out: Camera physically moves away from subject. Reveals more context, creates distance, or shows isolation. Different feel than zoom out.
cameraMovements.Dolly Zoom (Vertigo Effect): Dolly and zoom in opposite directions simultaneously. Creates disorienting effect. Famous in thriller and horror films.
cameraMovements.Tracking Shot: Camera follows subject laterally, usually on tracks. Keeps subject in frame while showing movement through space. Very cinematic.
cameraMovements.Trucking Shot: Camera moves sideways, parallel to action. Similar to tracking but usually perpendicular to subject movement.
cameraMovements.Arc Shot: Camera moves in a circular path around subject. Shows subject from multiple angles, creates dramatic effect, adds production value.
cameraMovements.Crane Shot: Camera mounted on crane moves up, down, or sweeping. Creates dramatic reveals, shows scale, or provides unique perspectives.
cameraMovements.Boom Shot: Vertical crane movement, camera rises or lowers. Often used for dramatic reveals or to show changing perspective.
cameraMovements.Handheld Camera: Camera held by operator without stabilization. Creates documentary feel, intensity, or chaos. Adds realism and energy.
cameraMovements.Steadicam Shot: Stabilized handheld camera movement. Smooth, flowing shots while following action. Combines mobility with stability.
cameraMovements.Follow Shot: Camera follows subject through space. Maintains consistent framing while subject moves. Creates engagement and momentum.
cameraMovements.Whip Pan: Extremely fast pan creating motion blur. Used for transitions, sudden direction changes, or energetic effect.
cameraMovements.Push In: Slow dolly toward subject. Builds tension, draws focus, or emphasizes emotion. More subtle than quick zoom.
cameraMovements.Pull Out: Slow dolly away from subject. Creates distance, reveals context, or shows isolation. Often used for emotional moments.
cameraMovements.Pedestal Up: Camera moves vertically upward on a fixed support. Follows rising action or changes perspective.
cameraMovements.Pedestal Down: Camera moves vertically downward on a fixed support. Follows descending action or changes viewpoint.
cameraMovements.Random Movement: Unpredictable, chaotic camera motion. Creates disorientation, panic, or documentary realism. Common in action scenes.
cameraMovements.Static Shot: Camera completely still, no movement. Creates stability, allows focus on performance, or builds tension through stillness.
cameraMovements.Gimbal Shot: Camera on motorized stabilizer. Allows smooth, flowing movement in any direction. Very versatile and cinematic.
cameraMovements.Slider Shot: Camera moves along a short track. Creates smooth lateral or forward movement. Adds production value to simple shots.
cameraMovements.Jib Shot: Camera on small crane or jib arm. Allows smooth vertical and arcing movements. More compact than full crane.
cameraMovements.Orbit Shot: Camera circles completely around subject. Shows subject from all angles, creates dramatic emphasis or time passage effect.
cameraMovements.Reveal Shot: Camera movement that gradually shows previously hidden elements. Creates surprise, introduces new information dramatically.
cameraMovements.Walk and Talk: Camera follows characters walking and conversing. Common in TV and film, maintains energy during dialogue scenes.
cameraMovements.Parallax Effect: Foreground and background move at different speeds. Creates depth and dimensionality. Very cinematic and engaging.
cameraMovements.Camera Shake: Intentional camera vibration or shaking. Simulates impact, explosion, earthquake, or adds intensity to action scenes.

cameraModels.RED Komodo: RED Komodo camera - Compact cinema camera with 6K resolution. Popular for indie films and music videos. Netflix approved.
cameraModels.Blackmagic Pocket 6K: Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6K - Affordable cinema camera with RAW recording. Popular among indie filmmakers.
cameraModels.Sony Venice: Sony Venice camera - High-end cinema camera used in major productions. Dual ISO sensor for low light performance.
cameraModels.Canon C300: Canon C300 Mark III camera - Professional cinema camera with excellent autofocus. Used for documentaries and commercial work.
cameraModels.Panasonic Lumix GH5: Panasonic Lumix GH5 camera - Hybrid mirrorless camera popular for video. 4K 60fps, in-body stabilization.
cameraModels.iPhone: iPhone camera - Modern iPhones shoot 4K video with computational photography. Accessible, always-in-pocket filmmaking.
cameraModels.GoPro: GoPro action camera - Ultra-wide angle, rugged action camera. Perfect for extreme sports and POV shots.
cameraModels.DJI Osmo: DJI Osmo gimbal camera - Handheld stabilized camera. Smooth motion, great for travel and run-and-gun shooting.
cameraModels.Bolex H16: Bolex H16 16mm film camera - Classic Swiss film camera. Distinctive vintage film aesthetic, used by students and artists.
cameraModels.Super 8mm: Super 8mm film camera - Vintage home movie format. Dreamy, nostalgic grain and color. Wes Anderson favorite.

cameraModels.VHS Camcorder: VHS Camcorder - 1980s-90s consumer video format. Lo-fi, nostalgic aesthetic with tracking artifacts and low resolution.

cameraModels.CCTV: CCTV security camera - Surveillance camera aesthetic. Low resolution, wide angle, often black and white. Creates tension and voyeurism.
cameraModels.Drone Camera: Drone camera - Aerial cinematography platform. Sweeping establishing shots and unique perspectives impossible from ground.
cameraModels.Panavision: Panavision camera - Legendary cinema camera system. Used in countless Hollywood classics. Premium rental-only cameras.
cameraModels.Aaton LTR: Aaton LTR 16mm camera - French documentary camera. Lightweight, quiet, perfect for intimate documentary work.
cameraModels.Cinema Vérité: Cinema Vérité style camera - Documentary realism approach. Handheld, natural light, observational style.
cameraModels.Found Footage: Found footage style camera - Amateur camera aesthetic. Shaky, low quality, creates authenticity and immediacy.

lightingArtificial.Artificial Light: Using man-made light sources (LEDs, tungsten, HMI). Complete control but requires equipment and power.
lightingArtificial.Bottom Lighting: Light coming from below subject. Unnatural, creepy effect. Classic for horror or creating unsettling mood.
lightingArtificial.Bounce Light: Light reflected off surfaces to fill shadows softly. Creates natural, soft fill lighting.
lightingArtificial.Candlelight: Warm, flickering light from candles. Romantic, intimate, or historical setting. Soft and flattering.
lightingArtificial.Chiaroscuro: Extreme contrast between light and dark. Dramatic, artistic style from Renaissance painting. Very theatrical.
lightingArtificial.Cinematic Lighting: Professional, carefully crafted lighting with depth and mood. Creates film-quality aesthetic.
lightingArtificial.Colored Gel Lighting: Lights with colored filters. Creates mood, atmosphere, or stylized looks. Popular in music videos.
lightingArtificial.Dramatic Lighting: High contrast lighting emphasizing mood and emotion. Strong shadows and selective illumination.
lightingArtificial.Fill Light: Secondary light used to soften shadows created by key light. Controls contrast ratio.
lightingArtificial.Film Noir Lighting: High contrast, dramatic shadows, often venetian blind patterns. Mystery, danger, moral ambiguity.
lightingArtificial.Firelight: Orange, flickering light from fire. Warm, primitive, or cozy feeling. Creates movement and atmosphere.
lightingArtificial.Fog/Haze: Atmospheric particles making light beams visible. Adds depth, atmosphere, and drama to lighting.
lightingArtificial.High Key Lighting: Bright, even lighting with minimal shadows. Creates cheerful, optimistic mood. Common in comedies and commercials.
lightingArtificial.Key Light: Main, primary light source for the scene. Establishes the overall lighting direction and mood.
lightingArtificial.Low Key Lighting: Dramatic lighting with strong shadows and contrast. Creates mystery, drama, or danger. Common in noir and thrillers.
lightingArtificial.Moonlight: Cool, blue-toned light simulating moon. Creates nighttime atmosphere. Often actually blue-filtered daylight or artificial.
lightingArtificial.Motivated Lighting: Artificial lights designed to look natural or sourced. Light appears to come from logical source in scene.
lightingArtificial.Neon Lighting: Colorful, electric neon signs or tubes. Creates modern, urban, or retro atmosphere. Popular in cyberpunk aesthetic.
lightingArtificial.Night Time: Low light conditions after dark. Requires artificial lighting or high ISO. Creates mystery, danger, or intimate moods.
lightingArtificial.Practical Lighting: Light sources visible in frame (lamps, candles, etc.). Makes scenes feel realistic and motivated.
lightingArtificial.Streetlight: Orange or white light from street lamps. Urban nighttime feel. Creates pools of light and shadow.
lightingArtificial.Studio Lighting: Controlled artificial lights in a studio setting. Complete control over direction, intensity, and color of light.
lightingArtificial.Three-Point Lighting: Classic setup: key light, fill light, back light. Standard for interviews and portraits. Creates depth and dimension.
lightingArtificial.Underwater Light: Unique quality of light beneath water surface. Blue-green tones, caustic patterns, soft diffusion.
lightingArtificial.Volumetric Lighting: Visible light beams through atmosphere (fog, dust, smoke). Creates depth and atmosphere. Very cinematic.

lightingNatural.Afternoon Light: Bright, harsh overhead light during midday. Strong shadows, high contrast. Can be challenging but creates specific mood.
lightingNatural.Ambient Light: General, overall light filling the scene. Base level illumination before adding dramatic lights.
lightingNatural.Backlit: Light source behind subject, facing camera. Creates silhouettes or rim lighting. Dramatic and artistic effect.
lightingNatural.Blue Hour: Cool, blue-toned light just before sunrise or after sunset. Creates moody, atmospheric scenes. Great for cityscapes.
lightingNatural.Dawn: Early morning before full sunrise. Soft, diffused light with cool tones. Peaceful, fresh, hopeful feeling.
lightingNatural.Diffused Light: Light scattered or softened through material. Reduces harsh shadows and contrast. Flattering and even.
lightingNatural.Dusk: Transitional period between day and night. Deep blue skies, mixed natural and artificial light. Dramatic and atmospheric.
lightingNatural.Evening Light: Warm, golden light as sun lowers in the sky. Softer than afternoon, more dramatic than morning. Versatile and attractive.
lightingNatural.God Rays: Visible light rays breaking through clouds or gaps. Dramatic, spiritual, or awe-inspiring effect.
lightingNatural.Golden Hour: Warm, soft light during the hour after sunrise or before sunset. Creates beautiful, flattering glow. Most popular time for outdoor filming.
lightingNatural.Hard Light: Direct, undiffused light creating sharp shadows. High contrast, defined edges. Dramatic or harsh depending on use.
lightingNatural.Lens Flare: Light artifacts from sun or bright lights hitting lens. Can be artistic effect or technical issue. J.J. Abrams loves these!
lightingNatural.Morning Light: Soft, cool-toned natural light in early morning. Fresh, clean feeling. Good for outdoor scenes with gentle shadows.
lightingNatural.Natural Light: Using only available daylight, no artificial lights. Realistic, authentic feel. Cost-effective but less control.
lightingNatural.Overcast: Cloudy sky creates soft, even lighting. No harsh shadows, flattering for faces. Good for consistent outdoor lighting.
lightingNatural.Rim Light: Light outlining the edge of subject from behind. Separates subject from background. Creates dimension and visual interest.
lightingNatural.Side Lighting: Light coming from the side of subject. Creates strong shadows on one side. Dramatic, emphasizes texture and depth.
lightingNatural.Silhouette: Subject completely dark against bright background. No detail visible on subject. Mysterious, dramatic, or artistic.
lightingNatural.Soft Light: Diffused light creating gradual shadows. Flattering, gentle, even. Common for beauty and portrait work.
lightingNatural.Sunny Day: Direct, bright sunlight. High contrast, strong shadows. Cheerful mood but can be harsh for filming.
lightingNatural.Top Lighting: Light coming from directly above subject. Creates shadows in eye sockets and under nose. Can be eerie or unflattering.

genrePresets.Claymation: Craft a scene in the distinct style of classic stop-motion claymation, emphasizing a subtly 'step-frame' or 'jerky' animation quality rather than smooth motion, to enhance the handcrafted feel. Feature matte, handmade textures and subtle fingerprints visible on all surfaces, giving it a tangible, sculpted feel. Utilize a diverse, slightly desaturated, yet clearly distinct and balanced color palette
genrePresets.Stop-Motion: A stop-motion cinematic close-up shot captures with jitter characteristic of stop-motion animation.
genrePresets.Macro Time-Lapse: An animated time-lapse of growing agar art inside a petri dish, macro lens, showcasing intricate microbial and fungi colonies forming a detailed moving animated bacteria.
genrePresets.Thermal Vision: An 8k high resolution shot captured in thermal vision with a glowing heatmap palette
genrePresets.Infomercial: A televised home shopping feature on a new product. A host introduces their new demo:
genrePresets.Space Archive: 90s USA space archive footage of a satellite with solar panels floating in the void, real footage, natural light, 8mm film texture sharpness color and focus
genrePresets.Film Noir: Black and white cinematography with harsh contrast, dramatic shadows cast from venetian blinds, femme fatale aesthetic. 1940s noir styling with rain-slicked streets reflecting streetlights, cigarette smoke drifting through beams of light. Low-key lighting creating deep chiaroscuro. High contrast between light and shadow, moody atmosphere.
genrePresets.Cyberpunk: Neon-lit dystopian megacity at night, holographic advertisements floating in mid-air, rain-soaked streets reflecting purple and cyan neon lights. Cybernetic enhancements visible, Asian-influenced architecture with towering skyscrapers. Flying vehicles streak past, tech noir atmosphere pervades. Blade Runner aesthetic with steam rising from grates, complemented by purple and cyan color grading.
genrePresets.Western Spaghetti: Wide desert landscape stretching to horizon, extreme close-ups of weathered eyes squinting. Dusty sepia and amber color palette, tumbleweeds rolling across barren ground. High noon showdown lighting casting stark shadows, Sergio Leone composition with dramatic zooms. Weathered leather and wood textures, desolate frontier atmosphere. Ennio Morricone-style dramatic tension.
genrePresets.Horror Gothic: Desaturated color palette draining life from the scene, thick fog rolling through decrepit architecture. Practical lighting from candles and oil lanterns casting dancing shadows. High contrast between light and darkness, cold blue color temperature. Crumbling stone and rotting wood textures, eerie silence broken by sudden sounds. Dread-inducing composition suggesting unseen threats.
genrePresets.Wes Anderson: Perfectly symmetrical composition with subjects centered in frame, pastel color palette of soft pinks, yellows, and blues. Whimsical production design with every object precisely placed, flat space camera movements tracking laterally. Quirky characters in vintage clothing, miniature aesthetic like a living dollhouse. Futura font for any text, meticulous attention to every visual detail. Deadpan performances.
genrePresets.Documentary Realism: Handheld camera work with natural shake and movement, available natural lighting without artificial sources. Observational cinema vérité style capturing authentic moments. Real locations showing genuine wear and use, ambient environmental sound. 16mm film grain texture adding documentary feel, unstaged spontaneous moments. Fly-on-the-wall perspective maintaining distance.
genrePresets.Sci-Fi Retro: 1970s-80s science fiction aesthetic with analog technology, CRT monitors displaying green phosphor text. Practical special effects using miniatures and models, blue screen compositing with visible matte lines. Grainy 35mm film stock, chunky physical interfaces with buttons and switches. Beige and gray color scheme, worn futuristic look suggesting well-used technology.
genrePresets.Magic Realism: Surreal fantastical elements appearing in mundane everyday settings, vibrant saturated colors especially in textiles and nature. Dreamlike atmosphere where impossible things occur naturally, symbolic imagery woven throughout. Latin American aesthetic with colonial architecture, golden hour lighting creating warm glow. Poetic visual metaphors, blurred boundary between reality and fantasy.
genrePresets.90s Camcorder: VHS tape quality with interlaced scan lines, date stamp overlay in bottom corner showing 1990s date. Auto-focus hunting in and out, oversaturated colors bleeding slightly. Motion blur during quick movements, low resolution creating soft edges. Home video aesthetic with nostalgic compression artifacts, tracking distortion occasionally. Consumer-grade image quality.
genrePresets.Found Footage: First-person handheld perspective with natural shake, shaky cam during moments of panic or running. Night vision mode showing green-tinted low-light footage, time code overlay in corner. Degraded video quality with digital artifacts, lens flares from direct light sources. Authentic panic captured, security camera angles showing wide surveillance views. Raw unedited feeling with abrupt cuts.
genrePresets.Silent Film: Black and white high contrast imagery, title cards with ornate borders displaying dialogue. Exaggerated theatrical performances with dramatic gestures, hand-cranked camera effect creating slight speed variation. 18fps projection feel making movement slightly jerky, vignette around edges darkening corners. Film grain and scratches showing age, German Expressionist influence in set design. Score direction suggesting piano accompaniment.
genrePresets.Giallo: Lurid saturated primary colors especially reds, yellows, and blues. Dramatic zooms into crucial details or faces, gloved killer POV shots stalking victims. Stylized theatrical violence with bright red blood, Italian horror aesthetic blending thriller and art film. Vibrant unrealistic color grading, psychological thriller elements with paranoia. Avant-garde editing with jarring cuts, prog-rock score direction with synthesizers.

templateExamples.Claymation Film: Wide frontal shot over a smooth concrete floor, set against a flat black background with harsh, directional lighting. At the center of the frame stands a standard blue portable toilet—weathered, dented, and visibly full, with warning stickers peeling at the edges. Suddenly, from the left, a full-size car bursts in at full speed—headlights off, engine roaring, tires barely gripping the concrete. Without slowing, it slams directly into the toilet. The structure explodes on impact. The plastic shell bursts apart instantly—walls collapse, the door blasts off, and the entire unit erupts into a violent spray of brown liquid, shredded paper, and blue chemical slosh. The car doesn't stop—it punches through the mess, dragging parts of the shell and loose debris with it, trailing a cloud of mist and foul residue. It exits frame to the right, its body streaked with filth, leaving behind a mangled heap of crushed plastic and fluid-covered concrete. Everything happens at real speed—brutal, fast, and final—captured in a single uninterrupted shot of spectacular chaos.

templateExamples.Action Destruction: Wide, static shot: gray concrete floor fades into black. One soft overhead pool reveals a giant clear water-balloon, brim-full, hanging centimetres above the floor. From left darkness a masked Mexican wrestler sprints in, boots thudding, cape snapping. He lowers his shoulder and slams the balloon; latex tears with a rubbery snap-pop. Instantly the sphere detonates—WHUMP—thousands of litres hammer concrete in a deep splash, glittering droplets hissing like shrapnel. The luchador resurfaces, mask plastered, boots squeaking across ripples. Shredded latex lies on the soaked floor. Only water drip and his breathing survive in the hush.

templateExamples.Thermal Vision: An 8k high resolution shot of a fast-paced first-person shot of a woman sprinting through a dense forest, captured in thermal vision with a glowing heatmap palette. The camera jostles as it weaves between towering trees, their trunks flaring in cool blues and purples against a warm yellow-green canopy pulsing with heat. Undergrowth flares in streaks of orange and red as branches snap aside, while faint white-hot flickers of fleeing wildlife—like deer or birds—dart through the frame. The runner's hands, glowing in bright crimson, push past vines, leaving smears of heat in their wake. Shot in a high-energy, immersive style with a jittery handheld feel, vibrant thermal heatmap gradients, and a faint digital grain overlay for texture.

templateExamples.Underwater Scene: An underwater scene of a large, slowly rotating Ferris wheel at a sunken carnival, with its lights still dimly flickering. The empty gondolas sway gently. The sound is muffled and deep, like a heavy blanket has been thrown over it. High-pitched frequencies are almost entirely absent, leaving only a low, resonant rumble and the creaking, groaning turn of the rusted machinery that's felt as much as heard.
templateExamples.Object Transformation: A continuous cinematic shot begins in a dim studio. At the center, a tightly closed flowerbud formed from torn plaid flannel and black leather sits like a defiant sculpture. Its surface is rough—frayed seams, visible stitching, and embedded metal spikes and safety pins. As the bloom begins, the petals flex outward in slow, fluid arcs. Shredded fishnet petals stretch, overlapping with weathered denim folds patched with raw slogans and DIY embroidery. Chains and studs emerge between the layers, glinting under hard light. The camera glides around the structure as zippers unfurl like coiled stems, their chrome sheen contrasting with the worn textiles. At the heart of the bloom, a central petal opens to reveal a flattened patch of punk ephemera—shards of vinyl, band insignias, and scratched metal. The final frame lingers on the bloom in full—a radical, asymmetrical construction, blooming not from nature but from cultural friction and reclaimed rebellion.
templateExamples.Explosive Organization: A wide-angle shot of a laundry room with a standard top-load washing machine with no frontal door stands centered in the room. The white machine with no window starts alone and closed, Suddenly, bang!, the top lid blasts open with explosive force, and a vertical burst of clean laundry fires into the air like a firework. T-shirts, pants, socks, and underwear shoot upward in tight arcs. As they fall, they begin to sort mid-air—each type of clothing grouping itself: socks land together in a neat pile, pants stack onto pants, shirts collect in a row, and underwear drop cleanly into ordered and folded piles. Items hit with speed but settle precisely, forming clear, categorized piles. The motion is fast, elastic, and deliberate. The camera pulls back, revealing a pristine, organized laundry station. At the center, the washer top lip remains opens, at it's base, piles of perfectly neat and ordered clothes.
templateExamples.Pop-Up Expansion: On a soft rug in a child's bedroom lies a large illustrated picture book, closed and pristine. The camera hovers above it as the book suddenly flips open, and—boom!—a colorful arc of miniature castles, model towns, toy soldiers, trains, and dragons explodes outward. Buildings unfold mid-air, a drawbridge slams down, and a tiny hot air balloon spins before landing atop a storybook mountain. Plush animals bounce into place beside trees and toy tents. The motion is whimsical, elastic, full of playful energy. The camera glides through the scene, revealing a miniature dreamworld built from stories. The book stays open at the center, pages fluttering slightly in the breeze.
templateExamples.Surreal Stacking: High-angle static shot of a chaotic massive, huge, incredibly high arch of plus size men and women and pool floats, precariously stacked in a huge indoor swimming pool. The people's bodies are positioned upright, sideways, diagonally, and tilted at improbable angles. The image has a photorealistic 35mm film look and realistic shadows, saturated colors emphasizing the precarious nature of the structure. The vastness of the pool where the arch of people and pool floats is accentuates the absurdity and surreal nature of the image.
templateExamples.Stop-Motion Character: A stop-motion cinematic close-up shot captures a charming scene. A trio of exquisite very fluffy and round baby snowy owlets, with their impossibly downy white feathers and enormous, endearing yellow eyes, are huddled together on a thick, snow-dusted tree branch. The owlets are meticulously crafted, their feathers appearing soft and exhibiting the subtle "boil" or jitter characteristic of stop-motion animation. The texture of the feathers should be palpable, almost like spun cotton. They blink slowly in unison and open their beaks to make gentle hoots, one owl at a time. The lighting is soft and ethereal, as if from a full moon, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the texture of their plumage and the rough bark of the branch. The color palette is subtle, with the pure white of the owlets and the dark greys and browns of the branch against a deep twilight-blue sky. The overall effect should be charming, whimsical, and slightly surreal, emphasizing the handcrafted nature of the stop-motion animation.
